key_insight: The paper gives the first full fixed-domain asymptotic theory for joint MLE of RBF-kernel GP variance, lengthscale, and nugget, proving consistency, rates, and asymptotic normality.
engineering_relevance: This provides principled guidance for how GP hyperparameters behave when data are densely sampled, improving confidence in model fitting for spatial, time-series, and scientific computing applications.
method: Analyze the joint MLE under fixed-domain asymptotics for an RBF Gaussian process.
Prove consistency and derive convergence rates for spatial variance, lengthscale, and nugget variance.
Establish joint asymptotic normality and show the rates are minimax optimal.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical asymptotic characterization of the MLEs rather than a data-driven benchmark evaluation.
watch_item: The results are specific to fixed-domain asymptotics with an RBF kernel, so behavior may differ for other kernels or increasing-domain regimes.
paper_title: Sharp Asymptotic Theory of Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Gaussian Processes with an RBF Kernel
